text:
Emma Chen: FYI — ACME is exploring a migration from CompetitorX to Redwood. They want a short POC to validate prompt parity, streaming behavior, and the token billing delta. Can we scope tech + commercial asks? cc @Raj Patel @Cameron Lee

Raj Patel: Happy to lead the technical side. Need: sample prompts, a few expected outputs (golden set), their current request/response patterns, and if they use any custom headers or session handshake. Do they have a proxy in front?

Cameron Lee: I'll own commercial. Quick question: they're ~1M tokens/month (mostly generation). Budget target is < $5k/mo. Ballpark for 1M gen tokens with our standard hosted pricing + light streaming? (we can refine after I get exact prompt lengths)

Raj Patel: Ballpark depends on average output length. Also quantization/beam use matters. For the POC we should run side-by-side with the CompetitorX endpoint to measure response deltas. Also need allowlist IPs for their staging env.

Lisa Morales: From infra: I can provision a small Dedicated pool for the POC (2 GPUs) so we can pin model version and avoid noisy neighbors. Need the seed prompt set (10–20), expected acceptance checks, and the IP ranges to allow. I can spin it up and share the staging endpoint.

Emma Chen: I'll collect the prompt set and acceptance criteria from their PM. They also sent a short security questionnaire — they specifically asked about KMS integration, data residency, and SOC2. @sec-bot any quick pointers?

sec-bot: Security note: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private deployments (via KMS integration), SOC2 Type II report available. For hosted, we offer encrypted-at-rest and encryption-in-transit; if they need dedicated key control we should propose Private with KMS. Link to report: https://redwood.example/reports/soc2.pdf

Raj Patel: For parity tests I'll create a harness that does side-by-side calls and computes similarity metrics (ROUGE, embedding cosine). Quick example of how teams usually call both endpoints for smoke: 
```
# competitorx example
curl -s -X POST https://api.competitorx.com/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer COMPETITOR_KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"prompt":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":128}'

# redwood example
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"input":"Summarize the following...","model":"redwood-1","max_tokens":128}'
```

Raj Patel: Also include a tiny adapter mapping note — CompetitorX uses `prompt` field, we use `input`, and streaming frames differ (they send full chunks then final). We'll normalize in the harness.

Cameron Lee: Proposed POC commercial plan: 30-day POC with $2k credit + standard per-token after. If they want Dedicated for the POC (for identical infra), require a short committed SOW/PO. I'll draft the SOW. Who's the billing contact?

Emma Chen: ACME legal gave us a PO template; billing contact is finance@acme.com. I'll forward. They asked about expected latency targets for customer-facing use (p95). Our target for baseline: < 400ms p95 for 128-token responses on Dedicated.

Lisa Morales: I can aim for endpoint + allowlist by EOD tomorrow. I will also provide a runbook with test endpoints, sample curl, and logs access.

Raj Patel: Acceptance criteria proposal (short):
- Response similarity: >= 95% agreement on intent/slot extraction for seed cases (or within acceptable delta on embedding cosine threshold).
- Latency: p95 < 400ms at test load (single connection).
- Billing delta: estimate cost delta within 20% of current spend for identical throughput.
- No PII leakage flagged in outputs.

Cameron Lee: LGTM. I'll attach pricing worksheet and send the credit approval. Also pinging legal to review SOW.

Emma Chen: Who owns the runbook and final acceptance report?

Raj Patel: I own the runbook and the A/B harness. ETA: 3 business days to get a first pass and run the 10 seed cases.

Lisa Morales: Infra owner here — I'll monitor the pool and collect latency metrics, share Grafana link.

Cameron Lee: I'll schedule a 30-minute sync with ACME for Wed 10am PT to kick off the POC. Emma, can you invite their PM and legal? :calendar:

Emma Chen: Done. Invite sent to sara@acme.com and legal@acme.com. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

Raj Patel: Quick action items: 1) Emma: send seed prompts + expected outputs; 2) Lisa: provision pool & endpoint; 3) Cameron: draft SOW & credit; 4) Raj: build harness.

Lisa Morales: Noted — will confirm IP allowlist and endpoint URL in this thread when ready.

Cameron Lee: Heads-up — ACME asked about tokenization differences (how we count tokens vs competitor). We should include a short note in the SOW about billing measurement and an example mapping.

Raj Patel: I'll produce a short note on tokenization and include a sample tokenization script and an example token count for a couple prompts.

Emma Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll update after the kickoff.

Cameron Lee: :rocket:
